title: Global trends of pandemic-prone and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks in 2024
snippet: In 2024, events of concern related to Oropouche virus disease were registered in 11 countries and territories, all of them reported in the Americas, particularly in Latin America and the Caribbean. While no outbreaks were reported in 2023, 2024 was characterised by the emergence of this disease in areas where it had not been previously detected, such as Bolivia, Cuba, the USA and Canada.8 9 [...] About 90% of the outbreaks in 2024 were associated with COVID-19, dengue, yellow fever, Oropouche virus disease and influenza (linked to identified zoonotic or pandemic influenza virus). Although disease outbreaks can affect any country anywhere, they tend to disproportionately occur in countries facing many other socio-economic development, climatic and humanitarian challenges. In this regard, sub-Saharan Africa and the subregion of Latin America and the Caribbean—home to just 23.3% of the [...] humidity and changes in precipitation patterns create breeding grounds that accelerate mosquito reproduction, leading to a higher risk of outbreaks. One of the most frequently recorded diseases in 2024 was the Oropouche virus. According to WHO, its spread has extended beyond its traditional geographical boundaries, driven by a combination of climate change, deforestation and rapid, unregulated urban expansion.
